correctness.rationale: For n=6m>=12 symmetry averaging reduces any feasible symmetric stochastic kernel to a circulant polynomial p(x) in x=cos(2pi j/n) of degree <=3 with p(1)=1. Proposed holding and step1/2 weights a=A/H, step3 b=c/H, A=(1-c)(1+2c), H=2c+5A. Direct independent symbolic expansion confirms p(x)+t=4b(x+1)(2x-1)(x-c+1/(2c)) and p(x)-t=4b(2x+1)(x-c)(x+1/(2c)), t=2b-a. The cited elementary trigonometric node inequalities place ALL discrete modes within [-t,t]. Four actual Fourier nodes c,1/2,-1/2,-1 equioscillate +t,-t,+t,-t, and the Lagrange interpolation signs at 1 force max|q| >= t for every cubic with q(1)=1; equality uniquely identifies invariant polynomial. The 1-t=6a Taylor expansion yields 18pi²/n². Independent full-matrix Fourier eigenvalue checks for n=12,18,30,60,102 agree to numerical precision. Non-invariant uniqueness is NOT asserted.
